clue.text: Comfort the distressed Icarus? Certainly not!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to console people in trouble
second meaning: Icarus, who flew too near the sun and fell, was certainly no sun expert

explanation.surface: A plea to console the boy who fell from the sky, met with a curt refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as SOL (Latin for sun) and ACE (expert): Icarus, whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun, was no master of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone in grief is to give them comfort, the verb sense of this word.

clue.text: "Quick shots" shouted up, having had too much fruit brandy?

indicators.text: shouted up, having had too much
indicators.note: the word is called out by someone who is up, merry from drink, and so slurred into a sh sound

parts.note: quick photographs are snaps

explanation.surface: A drinker calls for quick shots after already having too much fruit brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Quick shots suggests drinks; they are photographs, and a drunk shouting the word slurs it into the spirit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit distilled from fermented fruit, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Elgar's devilish clues will entertain, as will Firefly

definitions.note: a verb phrase: what a firefly will do, glow

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the jumbled letters hold the setter's word inside

parts.note: the word clues taken as written, ready to be jumbled

explanation.surface: The setter boasting that his fiendish clues will dazzle, like the TV show Firefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar is this puzzle's setter, so his own possessive is mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireflies glow with their own cold light, which is to emit light without heat.

clue.text: Edged with colour is a short baptismal robe

indicators.note: the word is has letters on both sides, bordering it
a is short of, missing from, the word for colour

the letter a, taken as written, is what the colour word drops
the word is taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like it describes the robe, but it says the colour word is short of the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom was the white cloth or gown put on a child at baptism.

clue.text: Cover for sword woun_'s healing crust?

parts.note: a scab is the crust that forms over a healing wound
the gap where the final D should be shows the word wound 'bar D', that is, without its D

explanation.surface: A puzzling typo-ridden note about a wound's crust and a sword's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The apparent misprint is the wordplay: 'woun_' is 'wound bar D', giving BAR D after the scab.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds and protects the blade of a sword.

clue.text: Crime Club rival's novel student's nicked from our bag

indicators.note: new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
stolen out of, so the student's letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.walkthrough: Bag is slang for one's interest or hobby, so our bag is crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setting and solving is the pastime of setter and solver; bag is slang for one's thing.

clue.text: Not have brown ales on shelf — the front of it's unsupported

indicators.note: in a down clue, the ales sit on top of the next letter
the word for have is not there, taken out of brown

parts.note: the word brown taken as written, from which the word for have is lifted
to have something is to own it
taken as written

indicators.note: it is the shelf, and its front is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of shelf, the 'it' of the clue

explanation.surface: A rule against having brown ales on the shelf, its front left unsupported.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end, describing a front without a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Going braless means wearing no brassiere, so the bust is not held up.

clue.text: Privately preferred track here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: said apart, so that others do not hear
second meaning: the main track on a single record

explanation.walkthrough: Split as A-SIDE, the side of a single carrying the featured song.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made in private; the A-side holds the record's lead song.

clue.text: Party for one enjoying escalating senior years

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: going up, so in a down clue the pair is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
at can mean attending, enjoying, as at a party

explanation.surface: A party thrown for someone revelling in their rising age.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is old age, especially when the mind weakens.

clue.text: Its home is New Road, where its scorer bats

indicators.note: crazy, as in bats in the belfry, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket club's home ground, where the scorer sits while its batsmen bat.
explanation.walkthrough: New Road in Worcester is the county cricket ground. 'Bats' looks like batting but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcestershire County Cricket Club plays home matches at New Road in Worcester.

clue.text: Trump laughs at this vibrating noise on Gold

definitions.note: Trump stands for an American, so the answer takes the US spelling

parts.note: a hum is a low vibrating sound
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a president mocking a buzzing sound on a gold surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is there only to signal an American, hence the US spelling without the U before the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy, the quality that makes people laugh, is spelt this way in American English.

clue.text: Producer of implant: kissing it moves saint …

indicators.note: only the saint, S, moves: it is shifted from inside the kissing word to sit between the I and T of it

parts.note: osculate means to kiss, so oscular is the adjective for kissing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye-implant maker caught kissing as a saint shifts position, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint gives S, and only that S changes place, moving from second letter to second-to-last.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocularist makes and fits artificial eyes, prostheses implanted in the eye socket.

clue.text: … minute implants activated in case of cognitive defect

indicators.note: minute implants itself, puts itself into the scrambled letters
the letters of in case are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing a story: a tiny implant switched on in a patient with memory problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activated' rearranges IN CASE into ANESIC, and M goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesic describes memory loss, a deficit in cognition.

clue.text: Backing instrument handled by Joe the Growler?

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read in reverse, as backing means going backwards
an instrument handled by someone is in their hands, so the soldier's letters go around it

parts.note: GI Joe is the archetypal American soldier, so Joe gives GI
a rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A backing musician plays an instrument for some gruff singer known as the Growler.
explanation.walkthrough: A growler is a small iceberg, so the definition is by example. Joe the Growler reads as a nickname, but Joe belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A growler is the name for a small floating chunk of ice, a little berg.

clue.text: Status attained by correspondence course?

definitions.meaning: read as a rank or qualification earned
studying by post: a master's degree gained by post

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as POST + MASTERSHIP: a master's degree earned by post, which is also the office of running a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or position of the person in charge of a post office.

clue.text: A host of drinkers celebrate secret bottles

indicators.note: the secret word holds the other inside it, as a bottle contains a drink

parts.note: inner, as in inner thoughts, means private
to keep a festival is to celebrate it

explanation.surface: Many drinkers celebrating while concealing bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A host of' looks like 'many', but host is a pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs a pub and is host to its customers.

clue.text: Cycling north, I perhaps fool press chief

indicators.note: 'Cycling' says letters at one end move round to the other end

explanation.walkthrough: I with DESSERT read upwards gives ITRESSED; cycling the final ED round to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a female editor, the head of a newspaper or press publication.

clue.text: Silly exploit precipitated by Basil?

parts.note: an exploit is a daring feat
basil is an example of a herb, hence the question mark
precipitation is rain, so precipitated means rained

explanation.surface: A foolish stunt pulled by a man named Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a person's name but is the herb; 'precipitated by Basil' gives HERB RAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherbrained person is scatty and foolish, the same as silly.

clue.text: Right lining for person employing pocket

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside, lining the word for

parts.note: to, as in a gift labelled for or to someone
a user is someone employing something

explanation.surface: Talk of the right material to line clothing for someone who uses pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Pocket is a verb: to trouser money is to pocket it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money, in British slang, means to take it for oneself, to pocket it.

clue.text: On the rise, Brooklyn Mutual Banks after a fall?

indicators.note: climbing, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
the words hold the answer as a bank holds deposits

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A New York savings bank's shares climbing after a market fall.
explanation.walkthrough: After means in the style of, and fall is the American autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumny describes something autumnal, in the manner of the season Americans call fall.

clue.text: So maybe Bow Church did soft targets?

indicators.note: as Bow, in the East End of London, would say it: Cockney drops its H

parts.note: a church had mass

explanation.surface: A church in Bow treating its congregation as easy pickings.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in Cockney London, where the initial H is dropped, so 'had mass' becomes 'ad mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The admass is the gullible public targeted by mass advertising, an easy audience.

clue.text: Very much like bilingual people?

parts.note: dig is slang for like or enjoy
lots is an informal way to say very much

explanation.surface: A question about whether one really enjoys people who speak two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A diglot is a person who speaks two languages, from Greek for two tongues.

clue.text: One source of unlikely tales about memorising bar noise

indicators.note: signals the letters of memorising are moved about
bar means except, so the letters of noise are excluded

parts.note: the letters named for removal from memorising

explanation.surface: A storyteller learns lines while the pub's din goes on around them.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, O, I, S, E out of MEMORISING and rearrange the remaining MMRIG. The Brothers Grimm collected fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm compiled German folk and fairy tales, fantastic stories hard to believe.

clue.text: Extremely supple, as those adding to roll do the splits

indicators.note: the word for what they do is split apart so that another word goes into the gap

parts.words: as those adding to roll do
parts.note: people adding names to a roll list them
the word the, taken as written, as the clue says to do the splits

explanation.surface: Gymnasts showing off their suppleness by doing the splits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do the splits' looks like a gymnastic move; in fact the roll-adders' verb is split open to take the word the.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful; the superlative is the most supple of all.

clue.text: A maiden confirms joints are joints in craft centre

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
IDs hips: identifies hips, which are joints, as joints

explanation.surface: A young woman confirming that cannabis joints really are joints, in a crafts centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Joints suggests cannabis cigarettes; here the joints are hips, and ID is a verb meaning confirm who or what something is.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a ship, the centre of the vessel or craft.

clue.text: Plant machinery primarily cored fruit

explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a factory alongside machinery, but it is the definition: a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, and trees are plants.

clue.text: Resistance group to the east of a certain county

parts.note: some, as in some person, means a certain one
a set is a group

explanation.walkthrough: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Stuff a little cough syrup shifted
